title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. The previous page sets up a dictionary for a single subgroup. 'Situation (1)' consists of three pieces of data: a group G, a normal subgroup 𝔊 ⊲ G, and a homomorphism φ_N : N → G whose composite to G/𝔊 is surjective. Put SN = φ_N^{-1}(𝔊). 'Situation (2)' is the intrinsic datum (𝔊, N, SN ⊲ N, φ_SN : SN → 𝔊, Θ : N → Aut(𝔊)), subject to compatibility conditions (3) a), b). These are presumably the usual ones: Θ|SN = Int∘φ_SN, and φ_SN(n s n^{-1}) = Θ(n)(φ_SN(s)). From (2) one rebuilds G as (𝔊 ⋊_Θ N)/{(φ_SN(s)^{-1}, s) : s ∈ SN}. This is the pushout of the extension 1→SN→N→N/SN→1 along φ_SN : SN → 𝔊. It has the following properties:
- 𝔊 maps onto a normal subgroup of G.
- N/SN ≅ G/𝔊.
- Ker(φ_SN) ≅ Ker(φ_N).
- φ_N is injective iff φ_SN is.
The last line of that page and the first line of this one state that (1) and (2) are inverse equivalences of categories, perhaps of 2-categories.

This page, part (b), generalises to a family. The datum (11) is G, a normal subgroup 𝔊 ⊂ G, and a family (φ_i : N_i → G)_{i∈I}, with SN_i = φ_i^{-1}(𝔊). Condition (12) asks that each composite N_i → G/𝔊 =: γ be surjective. For a reconstruction, Grothendieck proposes to start from (13): 𝔊 together with a family (N_i, SN_i, φ_i, Θ_i), each satisfying (3) a), b), where by (14) Θ_i : N_i → Aut(𝔊) and φ_i : SN_i → 𝔊. He wants to recover G 'from 𝔊 and the N_i' as a kind of relative amalgamated sum of the diagrams 𝔊 ←φ_i− SN_i ↪ N_i, with dashed arrows to G.

The next page corrects this. Each single i already reconstructs a copy G_i ≅ G, by the pushout above. To recover (11) one must add a transitive system of isomorphisms G_i ≅ G_j inducing the identity on 𝔊. This forces a transitive system of isomorphisms between the γ_i = N_i/SN_i, hence a common quotient γ, and then leads to a fibre product.

The likely motivation, given the 'équation des lacets' setting, is this: G is an arithmetic (profinite) fundamental group, 𝔊 the geometric one, γ the Galois group, and N_i local or decomposition-type subgroups (tangential base points, etc.). The aim is to describe the arithmetic group, and its Galois action on the geometric group, through local data attached to several 'points'.
errors: The notation φ_i is overloaded: in (11) it means N_i → G, in (12) the composite N_i → G/𝔊, and in (14) the restriction SN_i → 𝔊.

The proposed 'relative amalgamated sum' (15) is not well-defined as stated. A single (N_i, SN_i, φ_i, Θ_i) already determines G up to isomorphism, so the family alone does not glue without extra data: isomorphisms between the G_i over 𝔊, which are compatible with the identifications of the γ_i. Grothendieck himself corrects this on the next page.
In the profinite or topological setting the semidirect-product quotient construction needs the usual closedness and continuity checks; these are not mentioned here and are routine.

ideas.what: Equivalence between (G, normal 𝔊, N→G surjective onto G/𝔊) and intrinsic data (𝔊, N, SN, φ: SN→𝔊, Θ: N→Aut 𝔊), via G = (𝔊 ⋊ N)/SN
ideas.modern_name: Pushout (induced extension) of group extensions along a homomorphism; crossed-module / Schreier–Dedecker extension theory
ideas.where_published: Similar extension-theoretic manipulations appear in SGA 1 (Exp. XIII) and SGA 7-style discussions; unsure about this exact form

ideas.what: Reconstructing G from 𝔊 and several local subgroups N_i, with gluing data: a transitive system of isomorphisms between the G_i over 𝔊 and the common quotient γ
ideas.modern_name: Gluing/descent of group extensions; fibre product of extensions over a common quotient (cf. outer Galois representations and decomposition groups in anabelian geometry)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical group theory; the anabelian context is due to Nakamura, Ihara, Mochizuki and others

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine extension theory (pushout of extensions, semidirect product modulo an antidiagonal subgroup), used as a bookkeeping tool. The tentative 'relative amalgamated sum' is corrected by Grothendieck himself on the next page. There is no new result or connection beyond standard material.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 should read 'situations (1), et celle des situations (2).' — this matches the image.
In '(3) a) et b), — où bien sûr ∀i∈I', the '∀i∈I' is written to the right, on the same line as '(3) a) et b)'.
In 'Je veux justement la reconstitution', the reading of the second and third words is uncertain; the sense is 'Je veux faire/obtenir la reconstitution'.
The label before the final diagram is a crossed-out number (probably (15)), consistent with the next page reusing (15).
